column1: What is the formal object of Theological Anthropology (Antropologia Teologica)?
column2:
The human being considered in the light of divine Revelation: created in the image of God (imago Dei), wounded by sin, redeemed in Christ, and called to supernatural deification (theosis) and eternal communion with the Triune God.

🧠 Mnemonic: Remember the 4-fold Plot: **Creation (Image) -> Fall (Wound) -> Redemption (Christ) -> Glory (Theosis)**.

column1: What is the speculative distinction between 'quid sit homo' and 'quis sit homo'?
column2:
Quid sit homo (Nature/Essence): what man is as a rational animal (animal rationale), studied by biology, cosmology, and philosophy.
Quis sit homo (Person/Subject): the unique, incommunicable subject (incommunicabilis existentia) addressed by God by name and called into an I-Thou filial covenant.

🧠 Mnemonic: Quid = Quality of the species (What animal?); Quis = Question of the Subject (Who stands before God?).

column1: What is Boethius' classical definition of the person (De duabus naturis)?
column2:
"Persona est rationalis naturae individua substantia" (An individual substance of a rational nature).

🧠 Mnemonic: B-R-I-S: Boethius = Rationalis Individua Substantia.

column1: How does St. Thomas Aquinas refine Boethius' definition of the person (ST I, q. 29, a. 3)?
column2:
"Persona significat id quod est perfectissimum in tota natura, scilicet subsistens in rationali natura" (A subsistent individual in a rational nature).

🧠 Mnemonic: Boethius gives the Building block (Substantia); Aquinas gives the Act of existing (Subsistens: perfection of Esse).

column1: What Hebrew terms in Genesis 1:26 designate the 'image' and 'likeness' of God?
column2:
Tzelem (צֶלֶם): plastic image, concrete figure, statue/re-presentation.
Demuth (דְּמוּת): likeness, resemblance, abstract similarity preventing crude physical idolatry.

🧠 Mnemonic: Tzelem is Tangible (concrete statue); Demuth is Diffuse (spiritual resemblance).

column1: What distinction did St. Irenaeus of Lyons establish between 'image' (eikōn) and 'likeness' (homoiōsis)?
column2:
Image (eikōn): the natural, indelible constitution of man (rationality, free will, immortality of the soul) which remains after the Fall.
Likeness (homoiōsis): the supernatural robe of the Holy Spirit (grace, original justice) lost by Adam's sin and restored by Christ.

🧠 Mnemonic: Eikōn = Endures (human nature never erased); Homoiōsis = Holiness (supernatural robe lost and restored).

column1: What is the foundational Christological axiom of Gaudium et Spes 22?
column2:
"Reapse nonnisi in mysterio Verbi incarnati mysterium hominis vere clarescit" (In reality, it is only in the mystery of the Word made flesh that the mystery of man becomes clear).

🧠 Mnemonic: GS 22 = Mirror Principle: Adam is the shadow; Christ is the Mirror who reveals man to himself.

column1: What two epistemic contributions of faith to reason does John Paul II identify in Fides et Ratio 76?
column2:
1) Healing/Purifying (gratia sanans): cleanses fallen reason from the darkening effects of sin;
2) Stimulating/Guiding: proposes truths reason could have reached in principle but in fact had not (creation ex nihilo, personal God, spiritual soul).

🧠 Mnemonic: Faith gives Reason both Medicine (purifies sin's blindspots) and a Map (shows paths reason never took).

column1: How does Fides et Ratio 84 diagnose the postmodern mindset?
column2:
The claim that "the time of certitudes is irreversibly past; man must now learn to live in a horizon of total absence of meaning, all being provisional and fleeting."

🧠 Mnemonic: Postmodernity = The Cult of the Provisional: No truth, no anchor, only ephemeral drift.

column1: What is the full name, author, and date of the encyclical Magnifica Humanitas?
column2:
Pope Leo XIV, Encyclical Letter Magnifica Humanitas (May 15, 2026, 135th anniversary of Rerum Novarum), on the custody of the human person in the time of Artificial Intelligence.

🧠 Mnemonic: The 135 Leap: Leo XIII (1891) protected the worker from the factory; Leo XIV (2026) protects the person from the algorithm.

column1: What is the fundamental theological critique of the technocratic paradigm in Magnifica Humanitas?
column2:
It is an anti-human anthropology that views biological finitude, fragility, and mortality as engineering flaws to optimize away, reducing the person to manipulable raw material and discarding the vulnerable as 'sub-optimal.'

🧠 Mnemonic: Technocracy treats Fragility as a Bug to delete, rather than the Cradle of Grace to love.

column1: What is the distinction between Transhumanism and Posthumanism?
column2:
Transhumanism: uses biomedical technology and AI to enhance human capabilities and defeat mortality within the human condition.
Posthumanism: envisions an evolutionary ontological rupture into a synthetic, hybrid non-human species (cyborg).

🧠 Mnemonic: Trans = Tuning the human; Post = Passing beyond the human into machine.

column1: What is Rémi Brague's concept of 'cultural secondariness' (secondarité culturelle)?
column2:
The condition of Western Christian culture, which recognizes it did not invent its own origins, but remains perennially dependent on received, transcendent sources: Jerusalem (Scripture), Athens (philosophy), and Rome (law).

🧠 Mnemonic: The Christian J-A-R: Lives in humble secondariness from Jerusalem, Athens, and Rome.

column1: What are the two foundational cities identified by St. Augustine (De Civitate Dei XIV, 28)?
column2:
1) Civitas Terrena: built on love of self up to contempt of God (amor sui usque ad contemptum Dei);
2) Civitas Dei: built on love of God up to contempt of self (amor Dei usque ad contemptum sui).

🧠 Mnemonic: Terrena = Turn to Self (Contempt of God); Dei = Devotion to God (Contempt of Self).

column1: What is the theological symbolism of the Tower of Babel (Genesis 11)?
column2:
The human attempt to achieve absolute unity without God through technocratic uniformity: 'one language, one technology, one direction' to make a name for ourselves.

🧠 Mnemonic: Babel's Triad: 1 Language, 1 Tech, 1 Direction = Totalitarian Hive-Mind.

column1: Why was the confusion of languages at Babel an act of divine mercy rather than pure punishment?
column2:
It was a protective intervention (protectio misericordiosa) preventing mankind from cementing a totalitarian, dehumanizing monoculture that would eradicate personal freedom and diversity.

🧠 Mnemonic: Confusion of tongues was a Protective Firewall against monolithic tyranny.

column1: What is the Spanish theological neologism used by Pope Francis to describe God's initiative (Evangelii Gaudium 24)?
column2:
"Primerear" (El Señor nos primerea / Deus semper antevenit): God always anticipates, seeks, and encounters man first before man can seek Him.

🧠 Mnemonic: Primerear = God is always Previous! He steps onto the pitch before us.

column1: What does the theological myth of Sisyphus represent in modern anthropology (Albert Camus / P. O'Callaghan)?
column2:
The futile tragedy of autonomous human reason trying to solve the riddle of human destiny by human strength alone: pushing the boulder to the summit only to see it roll back down into existential absurdity.

🧠 Mnemonic: Sisyphus = The Pelagian Hangover: Autonomous climb -> Inevitable roll into the abyss.

column1: How did Friedrich Nietzsche unmask Enlightenment humanism in The Genealogy of Morals?
column2:
Nietzsche demonstrated that universal human equality and compassion are not self-evident rational truths, but Christian dogmas; once the Christian God is discarded, reason alone logically reverts to the aristocratic Will to Power and the domination of the strong.

🧠 Mnemonic: Nietzsche: Kill the Root (God) -> The Fruit (Equality) Dies! Only the Jungle remains.

column1: What did Aristotle teach regarding 'natural slavery' in Politics Book I?
column2:
He argued that some men are by nature slaves (physei doulos) because they lack the deliberative faculty (to bouleutikon) and possess only physical strength to obey, justifying their subjugation by rational masters.

🧠 Mnemonic: Aristotle's Biology Trap: No deliberative faculty = Natural slave by birth.

column1: What is the Thomistic definition of the union of soul and body (ST I, q. 76, a. 1; Council of Vienne, DH 902)?
column2:
"Anima intellectiva est unica forma substantialis corporis humani" (The rational soul is per se and essentially the single substantial form of the human body, constituting one unitary nature).

🧠 Mnemonic: Council of Vienne Validates Unica: Soul is the Unique substantial form of the body.

column1: What is the error of Cartesian substance dualism regarding man?
column2:
Descartes posited two completely heterogeneous substances: Res cogitans (thinking soul) and Res extensa (extended matter), reducing somatic life to a mechanical clock connected only externally via the pineal gland.

🧠 Mnemonic: Cartesian Ghost in the Machine: Two alien substances pinned together by a gland.

column1: What is John Locke's empiricist/functionalist definition of the person?
column2:
A thinking, intelligent being that possesses reason and reflection, and can consider itself as itself in different times and places, strictly via active consciousness and memory.

🧠 Mnemonic: L-M-P: Locke locks Personhood to Memory and current consciousness.

column1: Why is Peter Singer's utilitarian definition of personhood lethal to vulnerable humans?
column2:
Because he defines personhood by present functional capacity (sentience, pain/pleasure perception, rationality); consequently, human infants, the comatose, and severe dementia patients are non-persons, while mature non-human animals are granted personal status.

🧠 Mnemonic: Singer's Scalpel: Slaughters sleeping/infant humans, promotes conscious chimpanzees.

column1: What is Zygmunt Bauman's anthropological metaphor for postmodern man?
column2:
The 'Liquid Tourist' (l'eterno turista): a nomad of transient experiences who avoids all permanent, definitive commitments (fidelity, vocation, dogma, politics) to remain perpetually unencumbered.

🧠 Mnemonic: Liquid Tourist: Lives out of a suitcase; changes spouses and morals like hotel rooms.

column1: What is the theological significance of Christ assuming human nature 'sine peccato' (Hebrews 4:15)?
column2:
Christ assumed the full reality of human nature, including its mortal, passible condition (passibilitas et mortalitas), yet without sin, proving that sin is an unnatural parasite and not a constitutive part of being human.

🧠 Mnemonic: Sin is a Parasite, not human nature; Christ is 100% human without a trace of infection.

column1: Why is the Blessed Virgin Mary (Assunta) the eschatological archetype of redeemed anthropology?
column2:
Because in her, a purely human creature, every anthropological polarity (flesh/spirit, male/female, freedom/grace, mortality/immortality) is already fully reconciled, glorified, and deified by the Holy Spirit.

🧠 Mnemonic: Mary = The Anthropological Icon: What Christ is by nature, Mary reflects as redeemed creature.

column1: What was Pelagius' triad regarding human action (posse, velle, esse)?
column2:
Posse (capacity): given by God in human nature at creation.
Velle (willing) & Esse (acting): belong entirely to autonomous human free will without internal grace.

🧠 Mnemonic: P-V-E: Posse is Provided by God in creation; Velle and Esse are Vanishingly Exclusively man's.

column1: To what did Pelagius reduce actual grace?
column2:
External assistance: divine illumination of the Law and the moral example of Jesus Christ (exemplum Christi), explicitly denying internal elevating and healing grace.

🧠 Mnemonic: Pelagius reduces Jesus to a Sideline Coach, not an internal Life-Giver.

column1: What is the speculative distinction between gratia sanans and gratia elevans?
column2:
Gratia sanans: heals nature wounded by original sin (natura vulnerata) to overcome concupiscence and fulfill the natural moral law.
Gratia elevans: elevates human nature beyond its natural proportion to participate in the divine nature (2 Pt 1:4) and attain the Beatific Vision.

🧠 Mnemonic: Sanans Stitches the wound (Healing); Elevans Escalates to the Trinity (Deification).

column1: Can fallen man fulfill the entire natural law without grace according to St. Thomas (ST I-II, q. 109, a. 2)?
column2:
No. In the state of fallen nature (natura corrupta), man can perform individual natural goods, but cannot fulfill the whole natural moral law continuously without healing grace (gratia sanans).

🧠 Mnemonic: Fallen nature can win a Single Skirmish, but loses the Moral War without grace.

column1: What did the Council of Carthage (418, DH 225-227) define against Pelagius regarding grace?
column2:
Grace is not merely given so that righteousness may be fulfilled more easily, but is an absolute necessity so that what is good may be loved and done (ut diligatur et fiat).

🧠 Mnemonic: Carthage = Can't do without it: Ut diligatur et fiat (That it may be loved and done!).

column1: What did the Council of Orange II (529, DH 371-377) define regarding the beginning of faith (initium fidei)?
column2:
Even the very desire for cleansing, the first movement of prayer, and the beginning of faith (initium fidei) are produced in us by the inspiration and infusion of prevenient grace (gratia praeveniens).

🧠 Mnemonic: Orange = Origin: The very first spark of faith is already pure grace.

column1: What is Søren Kierkegaard's concept of 'Den Enkelte' (The Single Individual) against Hegel?
column2:
The conviction that the single individual is higher than the universal (Hegelian State/History), possessing infinite transcendent value by standing directly before a personal God (coram Deo).

🧠 Mnemonic: Enkelte = The Exceptional Individual standing Erect before God, defying Hegel's hive-mind.

column1: Why is empirical science structurally blind to the final cause (telos) of human nature?
column2:
Empirical science operates by material and formal description of physical processes; it can describe the mechanism of biological life (quid), but cannot perceive the transcendent finality (quis coram Deo) and supernatural beatitude for which man was created.

🧠 Mnemonic: Science maps the Engine (What), but has no instrument to see the Destination (Who & Why).

column1: What are the two principal Pentateuchal traditions of creation in Genesis?
column2:
1) Priestly Tradition (P) - Gen 1:1–2:4a: cosmic, liturgical hymn over 7 days, creation by God's Word (Dabar), culminating in the Sabbath;
2) Yahwist Tradition (J) - Gen 2:4b–25: dramatic, earthly narrative, molding man from dust (adamah) and divine inbreathing (neshamah), Eden, loneliness, and creation of woman (tsela).

🧠 Mnemonic: P is Priestly & Pomp (Liturgical Hymn); J is Jahwist & Journey (Earthly Clay & Drama).

column1: What does the Hebrew verb 'Bara' (בָּרָא) uniquely signify in the Old Testament?
column2:
Absolute divine production without pre-existing materials (creatio ex nihilo). In the entire Hebrew Bible, Bara has strictly God as its subject. In Genesis 1:27, it is climactically repeated three times for the creation of man.

🧠 Mnemonic: Bara = Belongs to God Alone! Repeated 3x for man: Crown of creation.

column1: What is the difference between 'Bara' (בָּרָא) and 'Yatsar' (יָצַר) / 'Asah' (עָשָׂה)?
column2:
Bara: sovereign divine creation ex nihilo without materials.
Yatsar / Asah: fashioning, molding, or making from pre-existing matter (like a potter molding clay, Gen 2:7); can have human artisans as subjects.

🧠 Mnemonic: Bara = From Nothing; Yatsar = Potter's Clay.

column1: What was the royal meaning of 'Tzelem' (צֶלֶם) in the Ancient Near East and its Biblical democratization?
column2:
In the Ancient Near East (Egypt/Mesopotamia), a tzelem was a physical statue representing the King in distant provinces; only the King/Pharaoh was the 'image of god.' Genesis 1 democratizes this royal status: every single human individual is the living viceroy and statue of God.

🧠 Mnemonic: Tzelem = The King's Statue: Genesis tears down the Pharaoh's monopoly and crowns every human as God's statue.

column1: What is the theological function of 'Demuth' (דְּמוּת) alongside 'Tzelem' in Gen 1:26?
column2:
It acts as a safeguard of transcendence. Derived from damah (to resemble), it indicates that man is an image, but only according to an analogical likeness, preventing crude physical anthropomorphism and pantheistic confusion.

🧠 Mnemonic: Demuth = Distance & Difference: Man resembles God, but is NOT God.

column1: What is the theological significance of the divine plural 'Faciamus hominem' (Gen 1:26)?
column2:
God departs from the 3rd person command (Fiat lux) and engages in a solemn deliberation. Patristic and Thomistic theology sees here the internal council of the Holy Trinity: the Father creating man through the Son in the Holy Spirit.

🧠 Mnemonic: Faciamus = Family Council: The Triune Persons confer before molding man.

column1: What does the Hebrew wordplay between 'Adam' (אָדָם) and 'Adamah' (אֲדָמָה) signify?
column2:
Adam (earthling/humanity) is taken from the Adamah (arable red soil/dust): it underscores man's radical somatic fragility, creaturely dependence, and physical solidarity with the material cosmos.

🧠 Mnemonic: Adam from Adamah: From red clay you came, humble dust before God.

column1: What is the Hebrew term for the divine breath in Gen 2:7 and its theological meaning?
column2:
Nishmat Chayyim (נִשְׁמַת חַיִּים: breath of life): God breathed directly into man's nostrils, proving that human spiritual interiority and the rational soul do not emerge from matter, but are immediately infused by God.

🧠 Mnemonic: Neshamah = No-matter: Directly inbreathed by the Creator.

column1: What theological principle does Genesis 5:1–3 establish regarding the Imago Dei?
column2:
Filiation: God created Adam in His likeness (demuth), and Adam fathered Seth in his own image (tzelem) and likeness (demuth). To be in the image and likeness of someone means to be their true son/daughter.

🧠 Mnemonic: Genesis 5 = Family Tree: Image = Paternity. Adam is God's child by creation.

column1: How does Genesis 9:6 ground the absolute inviolability of innocent human life?
column2:
"Whoever sheds the blood of man, by man shall his blood be shed; for in the image of God has God made man." Murder is not merely a social injury, but a direct sacrilege against the Creator whose image the victim bears.

🧠 Mnemonic: Strike the Man = Strike the Image: Murder is ontological sacrilege.

column1: Why is a purely 'assimilative' model (imitating Christ externally as one might imitate Napoleon) insufficient in Theological Anthropology?
column2:
1) Divine Person: Christ possesses a divine person with an assumed human nature, not a human person; halting at his humanity leads to Christological reductionism.
2) Immediate Mediator: In Christ, we directly encounter the Father (Jn 14:9; mediatio immediata).
3) Sine Peccato: Christ is without sin (Heb 4:15), whereas fallen humans inherit original sin; we cannot copy Him by moral will without internal elevating grace.

🧠 Mnemonic: Christ is Not Napoleon: You can't just put on his hat and boots; you need His divine life and grace infused within.

column1: What is the theological significance of woman being created as 'Ezer kenegdo' (עֵזֶר כְּנֶגְדּוֹ) in Gen 2:18?
column2:
'Ezer (helper/rescuer): in the Old Testament, this term is overwhelmingly applied to God Himself as Israel's savior (e.g., Ps 121:2); it never denotes an inferior servant.
Kenegdo (corresponding to him): standing face-to-face as an ontological equal and partner.

🧠 Mnemonic: Ezer = Eye-to-Eye: Woman stands face-to-face with man with God-like saving partnership, not subservient beneath him.

column1: What does the Hebrew wordplay between 'Ish' (אִישׁ) and 'Ishshah' (אִשָּׁה) in Gen 2:23 signify?
column2:
"She shall be called Woman (Ishshah) because she was taken out of Man (Ish)." Before woman's creation, man is called ha-Adam (earthling). The specific title Ish (man/husband) only emerges simultaneously when encountering Ishshah (woman/wife), proving that sexual identity is co-originary and relational.

🧠 Mnemonic: Ish & Ishshah Echo: Man only discovers who he is when standing before woman in mutual gift (unitas duorum).

column1: What are the Hebrew terms for 'male and female' in Gen 1:27 (masculum et feminam creavit eos)?
column2:
Zakar (זָכָר — male): from root meaning 'to remember/pierce.'
Neqebah (נְקֵבָה — female): from root meaning 'to open/receive/hollow.'
Indicates that human nature is created with built-in somatic complementarity, ordered to reciprocal self-giving communion.

🧠 Mnemonic: Z-N Polarity: Zakar (initiating gift) and Neqebah (receptive embrace), reflecting the Trinitarian communion.

column1: Across the Hebrew Old Testament, how many times does the verb 'Bara' (בָּרָא) appear, and who is its subject?
column2:
Exactly 55 times. In all 55 occurrences, God is the sole and exclusive grammatical subject. It is never applied to human or angelic making.

🧠 Mnemonic: 55 Stars for God Alone: Bara has a 100% divine copyright.

column1: How does biblical dominion (Radah / Gen 1:28) differ from modern technocratic exploitation (Magnifica Humanitas)?
column2:
Biblical dominion (radah) is pastoral stewardship and priestly custody (abad and shamar, Gen 2:15): cultivating and protecting creation as God's vicar.
Technocracy views creation as brute, passive matter to manipulate for utility and profit without transcendent moral limits.

🧠 Mnemonic: Shepherd, Not Bulldozer: Radah is the King's pastoral staff, not the strip-mining machine of Babel.

column1: Is sexual differentiation and procreation in Genesis a consequence of the Fall (original sin)?
column2:
No. Sexual duality (masculum et feminam) and the blessing of fertility (crescite et multiplicamini) were instituted by God before the Fall (Gen 1:28). Procreation is human co-creation participating in God's primordial blessing.

🧠 Mnemonic: Blessing Before the Bite: Fertility precedes the Fall; sexuality and children are God's original artwork.

column1: What title does Pope Leo XIV apply to the Blessed Virgin Mary in Magnifica Humanitas regarding anthropology?
column2:
Mater Unitatis (Mother of Unity): Mary harmonizes all human polarities (body/soul, freedom/grace, finite/infinite) not by technocratic uniformity, but through the maternal communion of love in Christ.

🧠 Mnemonic: Mater Unitatis: Not a totalitarian factory stamp of sameness, but a maternal harmony of diverse gifts.

column1: What does Magnifica Humanitas highlight about Mary 'seeing the invisible' in the Magnificat?
column2:
Mary recognizes God's kingdom and victory as already operating in history ("He has cast down the mighty... exalted the humble") not despite her creaturely fragility, but precisely through it, confounding technocratic power.

🧠 Mnemonic: Magnificat Optics: The humble creature sees God's hidden victory where technocrats see only weakness.

column1: What is the theological paradox of man proclaimed in Psalm 8:4–6?
column2:
"What is man that you are mindful of him?... You have made him little lower than the angels (elohim), and crowned him with glory and honor." Man is physically minuscule compared to the cosmos, yet elevated as God's royal viceroy.

🧠 Mnemonic: Psalm 8 Paradox: A speck of dust in the cosmic telescope, yet crowned King on the throne.

column1: What is the distinction between 'Nefesh' (נֶפֶשׁ) and 'Ruach' (רוּחַ) in biblical Hebrew anthropology?
column2:
Nefesh (throat / vitality / living soul): concrete life-energy, desire, breathing creature (shared with animals).
Ruach (wind / breath / spirit): the transcendent divine power from God that animates, guides, and elevates man.

🧠 Mnemonic: N-R Ladder: Nefesh = Neck/Throat (earthly vitality); Ruach = Rushing Wind from Heaven (divine power).

column1: What does the Hebrew term 'Basar' (בָּשָׂר — flesh / Latin: caro) signify in biblical anthropology?
column2:
The entire human being viewed in his somatic fragility, mortality, transience, and weakness (e.g., "All flesh is grass", Is 40:6). In the Incarnation, "The Word became flesh (sarx/basar)" (Jn 1:14), assuming our mortal weakness.

🧠 Mnemonic: Basar = Biological Brevity: Fragile mortal existence that withers like grass.

column1: What is the function of the 'Heart' (Leb / Lebab — לֵב / לֵבָב) in biblical Hebrew anthropology?
column2:
Not the seat of mere romantic emotion, but the central organ of intellect, deliberation, conscience, moral decision, and personal covenant before God.

🧠 Mnemonic: Leb = The Cockpit: The control room of reason, conscience, and will, not just sweet feelings.

column1: Why does Catholic dogmatics reject the Platonic/Manichaean view that the body is a prison of the soul (sōma-sēma)?
column2:
Because God created the material body "very good" (Gen 1:31). The body is an essential constituent of the human person, destined for bodily resurrection, and sanctified by the Incarnation ("Caro cardo salutis", Tertullian).

🧠 Mnemonic: Caro Cardo Salutis: The flesh is the hinge of salvation; the body is a temple, not a prison cell.

column1: What does St. Paul designate by the term 'Huiothesia' (υἱοθεσία — adoption as sons) in Gal 4:4–5 and Rom 8:15?
column2:
The supernatural elevation wrought by the Holy Spirit whereby redeemed sinners participate in the natural, eternal filiation of Jesus Christ, crying "Abba, Father!" and becoming co-heirs with Christ of Trinitarian glory.

🧠 Mnemonic: Huios + Thesia = Son-Placing: The Spirit places us into the Son's seat at the Father's table.

column1: What four dimensions of human dignity are distinguished in the Declaration Dignitas Infinita (DDF 2024, nn. 7–9)?
column2:
1) Ontological Dignity: inalienable, belongs to being created in God's image; never lost.
2) Moral Dignity: refers to the free exercise of will; diminished or lost by doing evil.
3) Social Dignity: pertains to living conditions; wounded by poverty and injustice.
4) Existential Dignity: subjective perception of life's worth; threatened by despair and loneliness.

🧠 Mnemonic: O-M-S-E: Ontological (always there), Moral (choices), Social (society), Existential (inner feeling).

column1: Why can ontological dignity (dignitas ontologica) never be forfeited, diminished, or extinguished?
column2:
Because it is rooted in the person's constitutive being as an embodied spirit called into existence by God and redeemed in Christ; it does not depend on cognitive performance, moral uprightness, biological health, or social utility.

🧠 Mnemonic: Ontology is Inerasable: You cannot lose what is given by God's creative act of existence (Esse).

column1: What key anthropological doctrine does Sirach 17:1–14 teach regarding the human faculties and the Imago Dei?
column2:
God formed man from dust and clothed him with strength in His image, equipping him with interior faculties: counsel, tongue, eyes, ears, and a heart for understanding (v. 6), giving him the Law of Life so that man might praise the Creator and enter into covenant communion.

🧠 Mnemonic: Sirach's Sensorial Five: Eyes, ears, tongue, heart, counsel—given to praise the King and live the Law.

column1: What does Wisdom 2:23 reveal about the relation between the Imago Dei and human immortality?
column2:
"Deus creavit hominem inexterminabilem, et ad imaginem suae similitudinis fecit illum" (God created man for incorruption/immortality, and made him in the image of His own eternity/nature). Death is an alien intruder brought by the devil's envy (Wis 2:24).

🧠 Mnemonic: Wisdom's Eternity: Image = Incorruption (Aphtharsia). Death is an uninvited guest.

column1: In the Babylonian creation myth Enuma Elish, why and from what was mankind created?
column2:
Man was created from the blood of the slain rebel god Kingu mixed with clay, strictly to act as a labor slave to relieve the weary gods from manual work and feed them sacrifices.

🧠 Mnemonic: Kingu's Slave-Blood: Babylonian man is born a rebel slave; Biblical man is born a royal son.

column1: How does biblical creation in Genesis radically overturn the anthropology of the Enuma Elish?
column2:
In Genesis, there is no cosmic warfare, no demonic rebel blood, and no divine fatigue. Creation is sovereignly spoken in peaceful goodness (bara), and man is created not to be a feeding slave, but God's beloved covenant partner, viceroy, and friend.

🧠 Mnemonic: Peaceful Sovereign Word vs. Bloody Chaos: God needs no slaves; He shares His royal Sabbath rest.

column1: What is Plato's famous definition of human destiny in Theaetetus 176a-b?
column2:
"Homoiosis theo kata to dynaton" (Becoming like God as far as humanly possible), achieved by fleeing the earthly body and the material world through intellectual contemplation and philosophical justice.

🧠 Mnemonic: Plato Flees the Body: Likeness by escaping matter, whereas Christianity redeems the flesh (Caro cardo salutis).

column1: What famous formula did Tertullian write in De Resurrectione Carnis 6 regarding the creation of Adam from clay?
column2:
"Quodcumque limo exprimebatur, Christus cogitabatur homo futurus" (Whatever was being expressed in the mud, Christ was being thought of as the man to come!).

🧠 Mnemonic: Christ in the Clay: The Father didn't model Christ on Adam; He sculpted Adam looking at the future Incarnate Son.

column1: What are the two major speculative implications of Tertullian's insight that Christ was the model for Adam's clay?
column2:
1) Christ is the eternal Prototype: Adam is merely a preliminary sketch; Christ is the true Original.
2) Sanctity of the somatic body: Human flesh was designed from the beginning to be capable of bearing God in the Incarnation (capax Dei).

🧠 Mnemonic: The Body was Built for the Incarnation: Not an afterthought, but the divine blueprint.

column1: What did St. Irenaeus of Lyons mean by the 'Two Hands of God' in the creation of man?
column2:
The Son (Word) and the Holy Spirit (Wisdom). God did not delegate man's creation to angels or demiurges; God Himself fashioned man out of clay by the Son and breathed life through the Holy Spirit.

🧠 Mnemonic: The Father's Two Hands: Word fashions the clay, Spirit breathes the fire.

column1: In St. Irenaeus' theology, what was lost at the Fall, and what remained intact in human nature?
column2:
The Image (eikōn) remained (man retained rational nature, intellect, and free will); the Likeness (homoiōsis) was lost (the supernatural robe of the Holy Spirit, original justice, and filial communion).

🧠 Mnemonic: Eikōn stays, Homoiōsis flies: The human hardware endures; the supernatural Spirit-software was wiped until Christ reinstalled it.

column1: What is St. Irenaeus' foundational doctrine of 'Recapitulation' (Anakephalaiōsis / Eph 1:10)?
column2:
Christ, the true Image of God, summed up in Himself the entire history of humanity from Adam, retracing every stage of human life and reversing Adam's disobedience through His perfect obedience on the Cross, restoring the lost likeness.

🧠 Mnemonic: Recapitulation = Divine Rewind & Rerun: Christ rewinds Adam's tape and replays it in perfect obedience.

column1: Why do the Church Fathers insist that man was made 'ad imaginem' (κατ' εἰκόνα — according to the image) rather than being the Image of God itself?
column2:
Because Jesus Christ alone is the Image of the invisible God (Col 1:15; 2 Cor 4:4); man is not the absolute Image, but is created according to and directed toward that uncreated Image to be conformed to Him (Rom 8:29).

🧠 Mnemonic: The Mirror, Not the Sun: Christ is the Image; man is the mirror angled to reflect Him.

column1: How does Colossians 1:15 define the relationship between Jesus Christ, God, and creation?
column2:
"Qui est imago Dei invisibilis, primogenitus omnis creaturae" (He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation). In Christ, the transcendent, unseeable God becomes visibly manifest.

🧠 Mnemonic: Colossians 1:15 = The Visible Face: Christ is the visible Icon of the invisible Father.

column1: How does Romans 8:29 define the ultimate telos of the human person in God's eternal plan?
column2:
"Praedestinavit conformes fieri imaginis Filii eius" (He predestined us to be conformed to the image of His Son, so that He might be the firstborn among many brothers). The Imago Dei culminates in Trinitarian fraternity and filial divinization (theosis).

🧠 Mnemonic: Conformed to the Firstborn: Creation begins with clay in Adam; glory ends with brotherly conformation to Christ.

column1: What is the foundational Christological and anthropological formula of Gaudium et Spes 22 (§ 1)?
column2:
"Reapse nonnisi in mysterio Verbi incarnati mysterium hominis vere clarescit... Christus, novissimus Adam, [...] hominem ipsi homini plene manifestat eique altissimam eius vocationem patefacit." (Only in the mystery of the Incarnate Word does the mystery of man truly become clear... Christ, the new Adam, fully reveals man to himself and makes his supreme calling clear).

🧠 Mnemonic: N-A-M-P: Novissimus Adam Manifestat Patefacit (The New Adam Manifests man to himself and Patents his calling).

column1: How does Gaudium et Spes 24 (§ 3) define the paradox of human self-fulfillment?
column2:
Man is the only creature on earth that God willed for its own sake, but "plene seipsum invenire non posse nisi per sincerum sui ipsius donum" (he cannot fully find himself except through a sincere gift of self).

🧠 Mnemonic: S-S-D: Sincerum Sui Donum (Self-giving is the Secret to Discovering oneself).

column1: Why can natural human love (amor naturalis) never evolve linearly into supernatural charity (caritas infusa)?
column2:
Because of the infinite qualitative disproportion between creature and Creator. Even in unfallen Adam (status naturae integrae), caritas is an unowed divine gift (donum indebitum / donum superadditum) participating in the Holy Spirit. Claiming unfallen natural love is already supernatural charity is the condemned heresy of Baianism (1567).

🧠 Mnemonic: Baius Blurs nature and grace; Thomas Distinguishes amor naturalis (human will) from caritas (Holy Spirit's indwelling).

column1: Does Christ's redemption merely return humanity to Adam's unfallen status in the Garden of Eden?
column2:
No. As the Exsultet proclaims ("O felix culpa") and Romans 5:20 affirms ("superabundavit gratia"), redemption in Christ elevates man to an ontologically higher dignity: incorporation as living members of the Mystical Body of Christ (Corpus Christi mysticum) and adoptive sons in the Only-Begotten Son (filii in Filio).

🧠 Mnemonic: Adam had a Garden; the Christian has the Trinity.

column1: Why do Henri de Lubac and Paul O'Callaghan insist that Christian humanism must be a 'converted humanism' (humanisme converti)?
column2:
Because human self-realization cannot be achieved on natural, worldly terms. The Cross of Christ (crux Christi) stands as a stumbling block and folly (1 Cor 1:23) that crucifies the old man (vetus homo) and its self-idolatry, so that the new man (novus homo, Eph 4:24) can be born through metanoia.

🧠 Mnemonic: The Cross is the Crucible of Humanism: No Easter without Good Friday; no new man without dying to the old.

column1: What is Tertullian's famous formulation in De carnis resurrectione 8, 2 regarding the dignity of the body in salvation?
column2:
"Caro cardo salutis" (The flesh is the hinge of salvation). Since the Son of God took on flesh and was raised bodily, the human body is not a prison to escape, but the somatic hinge through which grace, sacraments, and eternal life enter man.

🧠 Mnemonic: Cardo = Hinge: The flesh is the somatic doorframe through which the Incarnation swings open into eternal glory.

column1: What two Hebrew verbs in Genesis 1:28 define human dominion over the earth, and how do they exclude despotism?
column2:
Kavash (כָּבַשׁ): to subdue, cultivate, and bring nature into orderly harmony.
Radah (רָדָה): to rule, shepherd, or exercise royal stewardship.

Biblical dominion is not tyrannical exploitation or arbitrary destruction: it is a priestly and royal stewardship reflecting God's providential care (cura pastoralis) over creation.

🧠 Mnemonic: Kavash Cultivates, Radah Rules like a Shepherd: Cultivate the soil (kavash) and shepherd the flock (radah); never exploit like a tyrant.

column1: What three creaturely boundaries did God institute in Genesis 1-2 to prevent human dominion from degenerating into despotism?
column2:
1. The Dietary Boundary (Gen 1:29): Originally granted a vegetarian diet, excluding arbitrary violence or slaughter.
2. The Moral Boundary (Gen 2:16-17): The forbidden Tree of Knowledge; creaturely autonomy remains subordinate to God's transcendent moral law.
3. The Liturgical Boundary (Gen 2:2-3): The Sabbath rest; work and economic production are not absolute ends, but subordinated to contemplation, worship, and rest in God.

🧠 Mnemonic: Diet, Tree, Sabbath: What you eat, what you obey, and when you rest.

column1: What profound truth regarding the imago Dei is revealed in Genesis 5:1-3 when Adam begets Seth 'in his own likeness, after his image'?
column2:
1. Filiation (Sonship): To be in another's image and likeness is the biblical definition of sonship. Adam being in God's image means Adam was created as the adoptive son of God (Luke 3:38).
2. Preservation Post-Fall: The imago Dei was not annihilated by the Fall; it remains ontologically intact and is transmitted across generations by natural propagation.

🧠 Mnemonic: Like Father, Like Son: Image = Filiation. Seth inherited Adam's image; Adam received God's image.

column1: Why does Genesis 9:6 strictly prohibit murder, and what does this prove about the post-lapsarian status of the imago Dei?
column2:
"Quicumque effuderit humanum sanguinem, fundetur sanguis illius; ad imaginem quippe Dei factus est homo" (Gen 9:6).

Murder is a direct sacrilege against God because every human being bears the divine image. This dogmatically proves that original sin did not destroy or erase the imago Dei in fallen humanity.

🧠 Mnemonic: Blood is Sacred because the Image Abides: To strike man is to strike the portrait of the King.

column1: In Genesis 1:26, why did the sacred author place both tzelem (plastic statue) and demuth (abstract likeness) in dialectical tension?
column2:
To establish a theological safeguard against two opposite errors:
1. Only tzelem: would collapse into crude physical anthropomorphism or idolatry (viewing man as a literal material idol of God).
2. Only demuth: would evaporate man's relationship with God into an ethereal, disembodied metaphor.

Demuth qualifies and spiritualises tzelem, while tzelem grounds demuth in concrete bodily representation.

🧠 Mnemonic: Statue (Tzelem) + Similitude (Demuth): Concrete enough to act on earth, spiritual enough not to be an idol.

column1: What are the five salvific links of the Pauline Catena Aurea in Romans 8:29-30?
column2:
1. Foreknowledge (Proegnō / Praescivit): Eternal loving election in Christ.
2. Predestination (Proōrisen / Praedestinavit): Conformed to the image of the Son (filii in Filio).
3. Vocation (Ekalesen / Vocavit): Historical summons through Gospel and grace.
4. Justification (Edikaiōsen / Iustificavit): Ontological renewal from sin to divine adoption.
5. Glorification (Edoxasen / Glorificavit): Eschatological beatitude and resurrection of the flesh.

🧠 Mnemonic: F-P-V-J-G (The Golden Staircase): Foreknown -> Predestined -> Vocation -> Justification -> Glorification.

column1: What are the three constitutive dimensions of Catholic predestination that refute the Calvinist 'decretum horribile'?
column2:
1. Theological: God possesses a Universal Salvific Will (1 Tim 2:4: "omnes homines salvos fieri vult"); absolute gratuitous priority of grace.
2. Christological: Christ is the archetype and first object of predestination (1 Pet 1:20); all are elected exclusively in Christo.
3. Ecclesiological: Election is corporate and mediated through the Church (Eph 1:4: "elegit nos in ipso"), requiring free, synergistic cooperation.

🧠 Mnemonic: God Wills All, Christ Leads All, Church Gathers All: Father's will, Son's archetype, Church's body.

column1: How did the Council of Quierzy (853 AD, DH 621-624) dogmatically define predestination against the double predestination of Gottschalk?
column2:
1. Single Predestination: God predestined the elect to eternal life by grace, but predestined no one to eternal damnation (foreknowing, but not predetermining, evil).
2. Universal Salvific Will: Almighty God wills all men without exception to be saved (1 Tim 2:4).
3. Universal Atonement: Christ suffered and died for all human beings without exception; those who perish do so solely through their own guilty refusal of grace.

🧠 Mnemonic: Quierzy Clears the Cross: No double doom; Christ died for all, damnation is self-inflicted.

column1: What are the four complementary levels of Christian Vocation according to contemporary Catholic theological anthropology?
column2:
1. Vocatio ad esse (Call to Existence): Gaudium et Spes 19; creation ex nihilo is an address of personal love calling man into dialogue.
2. Vocatio ad Ecclesiam (Call to the Church): Baptismal incorporation and the Universal Call to Holiness (Lumen Gentium V).
3. Vocatio specifica (Specific Vocation): Public ecclesial state of life (priesthood, religious life, matrimony, apostolic secular celibacy).
4. Missio personalis (Personal Mission): The unique, unrepeatable historical task entrusted to the concrete individual.

🧠 Mnemonic: Being -> Baptism -> State -> Mission: Exist as man, enter the Church, choose your state, fulfil your mission.

column1: What are the four constitutive dimensions of the Universal Call to Holiness articulated in Lumen Gentium chapter V?
column2:
1. Subjective: Addressed to every baptised person without aristocratic exception (not reserved for monks or clergy).
2. Objective: Realised within and through all secular conditions: work, marriage, sickness, youth, old age.
3. Ecumenical: The common baptismal root and unifying ultimate telos shared by all separated Christians.
4. Cosmic: The sanctification and consecration of temporal institutions, culture, and material creation (recapitulatio in Christo).

🧠 Mnemonic: S-O-E-C (The Holiness Spectrum): Subject (who), Object (where), Ecumenical (with whom), Cosmic (for the universe).

column1: Why is the popular analogy of God as a 'Divine GPS' an erroneous temporal anthropomorphism in the theology of vocation?
column2:
Because it assumes God operates in temporal succession: waiting for man to sin or err, being caught off guard, and scrambling to 'recalculate' a secondary Plan B or C.

In reality, God's eternal decree (tota simul possessio) encompasses all time. Within sovereign providence, creaturely free decisions are embraced ab aeterno and genuinely co-configure and shape the historical reality of the vocation itself.

🧠 Mnemonic: God is not a TomTom: No recalculating routes; human freedom is embraced within eternal providence.

column1: What is the epistemic distinction between the certainty one possesses regarding the Universal Call to Holiness vs. a Specific Vocation?
column2:
1. Certitude of Faith (Certitudo Fidei): Pertains to the universal call to existence and holiness in the Church; it is revealed by God and held with absolute theological certainty.
2. Moral Certitude (Certitudo Moralis): Pertains to one's specific state of life and concrete personal mission; it is achieved not by revelation or mathematical deduction, but through spiritual discernment, prayer, and reading the providential signs of one's history.

🧠 Mnemonic: Faith for the Goal, Moral Prudence for the Road: Certain by faith that I must be holy; morally certain by discernment how I must live it.

column1: How did the Council of Trent (Session VI, cap. 7, DH 1528) dogmatically define the nature of Justification against forensic imputation?
column2:
"Iustificatio... non est sola peccatorum remissio, sed et sanctificatio et renovatio interioris hominis per voluntariam susceptionem gratiae et donorum, unde homo ex iniusto fit iustus, et ex inimico amicus, ut sit heres secundum spem vitae aeternae."

Justification is not a legal fiction or external cover (Luther's imputatio), but an ontological translation from the state of sin (status peccati) to the state of grace and adoptive filiation (status gratiae).

🧠 Mnemonic: Remission + Renewal: Not just pardoned, but regenerated from enemy to friend.

column1: How did the early Church Fathers utilize the reality of Deification (Theosis, 2 Peter 1:4) to demonstrate the true divinity of Jesus Christ?
column2:
Foundational Patristic Axiom: "Deus homo factus est, ut homo fieret Deus" (St. Irenaeus, St. Clement of Alexandria, St. Athanasius).

The Argument: No creature, angel, or prophet can impart uncreated divine life or make man a partaker of the divine nature (consortes divinae naturae). If Christ truly deifies believers, Christ Himself must be consubstantially and truly God.

🧠 Mnemonic: Only God can Divinize: A creature cannot give uncreated life; since Christ deifies us, Christ is God.

column1: Distinguish Gratia Sanans from Gratia Elevans, and explain why Adam required Gratia Elevans even before original sin.
column2:
1. Gratia Sanans (Healing Grace): Heals the wounds of sin, remits guilt, and restores integrity to fallen human faculties.
2. Gratia Elevans (Elevating Grace): Ontologically raises created human nature above its native biological capacities into supernatural Trinitarian life.

Adam's Need: Even in the state of unfallen innocence (status naturae integrae), human nature as a created finite substance has no natural capacity to attain the Beatific Vision. Communion with God is always an unmerited, supernatural gift.

🧠 Mnemonic: Sanans Heals the Wound; Elevans Climbs to the Trinity: Adam had no wound, but still needed the ladder.

column1: How does Catholic dogma (Trent, Session V and VI, DH 1515) distinguish concupiscence from formal sin against Martin Luther?
column2:
Martin Luther: Identified concupiscence with original sin itself, claiming man remains totally corrupt and permanently sinful even after baptism (simul iustus et peccator).

Catholic Dogma: Baptism truly destroys original sin. Concupiscence (fomes peccati) remains in the baptised not as sin, but as a disordered inclination left for ascetical struggle (ad agonem relicta). It cannot harm those who do not consent, but resist it through Christ's grace.

🧠 Mnemonic: Inclination is not Consent: The spark (fomes) is not the fire until the will fans it.

column1: What was the core error of Pelagianism regarding human nature, original sin, and the role of grace?
column2:
Pelagius was a moral rationalist who argued that human nature remains intact and fully capable of fulfilling all divine commands without internal grace:
1. Nature: Free will is morally autonomous and uninjured.
2. Original Sin: Merely a bad example (malum exemplum Adae), transmitted by imitation (per imitationem), not generation.
3. Grace: Reduced to external law, Gospel instruction, or an optional 'vitamin supplement' that makes virtue easier but is not strictly necessary.

🧠 Mnemonic: Pelagius' Vitamin Shot: Nature is healthy, Adam was just a bad model, grace is an optional supplement.

column1: What was St. Augustine's speculative breakthrough in De diversis quaestionibus ad Simplicianum (397 AD) regarding the initium fidei?
column2:
Prior to 397 AD, Augustine held that while grace was needed to live well, the very first impulse of faith (initium fidei: deciding to believe and ask for help) belonged autonomously to human free will.

Meditating on 1 Corinthians 4:7 ("Quid habes quod non accepisti?"), Augustine realised that even the very first desire for faith and conversion is an unmerited gift of prevenient grace (gratia praeveniens).

🧠 Mnemonic: Grace Conquered Free Will: "I laboured for free will, but the grace of God conquered" (Retractationes).

column1: What famous prayer of St. Augustine in Confessions X scandalized Pelagius, and what dogmatic truth does it encapsulate?
column2:
"Da quod iubes et iube quod vis" (Grant what You command, and command what You will).

Dogmatic Truth: God's moral precepts are not burdens imposed upon autonomous human willpower; they are gifts that God Himself accomplishes in the creature through sanctifying and operative grace. When God crowns our merits, He crowns His own gifts.

🧠 Mnemonic: Give what You Command: God provides the grace before demanding the obedience.

column1: How did the Second Council of Orange (529 AD, DH 371-397) decisively resolve the Semi-Pelagian controversy?
column2:
Confirmed by Pope Boniface II, Orange II defined the absolute necessity of prevenient grace (gratia praeveniens) across all stages of salvation:
1. Before: Man cannot even desire, believe, pray, or seek salvation without the prior infusion of the Holy Spirit (canons 3-7).
2. During: Grace accomplishes interior justification and remission of sin.
3. After: The justified constantly require the special gift of perseverance (donum perseverantiae) to endure until death.

🧠 Mnemonic: Prevenient, Justifying, Persevering: Grace before the step, grace during the step, grace to cross the finish line.
